baseline_reason: Every divergence below the excused ones predates the gate and each needs its own decision, so --strict fails on a rise rather than demanding zero. Lower this number whenever a divergence is closed; the gate fails on a drop too, so an improvement cannot be silently spent. Items 31-37 of the cleanup plan are scoped from this report. The unit is one module, never one directory: a one-sided directory counts once per module inside it, so it cannot absorb new modules without moving the number. An excused directory is the deliberate exception -- it excuses its whole subtree, because the excuse is that there is no counterpart to mirror, which makes growth inside it expected rather than drift.

python_only.runtime/python/host: The `with ws:` entry point: the host interpreter's own builtins.open, io.open and os functions patched onto a workspace (fs, open, file, list, stat, constants), plus the re-entrancy bypass (host_io) the mount path sets so a backend serving an op reaches the host. Both ride the runtimes' file API (runtime/files RuntimeFiles) over ws.vfs. Its node twin is runtime/js/host (fs, constants, descriptors, list and stat, excused there): an npm consumer holds promises, not file objects, so file and open have nothing to mirror, and node needs no host_io because the patch swaps only the CommonJS fs and fs.promises functions, which every node backend's ESM node:fs/promises import never reaches (pinned by fs.test.ts, 'a disk root at its own prefix does not re-enter').
python_only.bridge: sync.py exists to run an event loop on a worker thread for the FUSE callbacks, which python needs because its FUSE loop is threaded and node's is not.
python_only.agents/agno: Ecosystem split: agno is a python-only framework.
python_only.agents/pydantic_ai: Ecosystem split: pydantic-ai is a python-only framework.
python_only.runtime/python/wasi: CPython on Wasmtime is a Python host adapter. TypeScript hosts CPython through Pyodide, whose engine-specific subtree is excused separately.

typescript_only.runtime/python/pyodide: Pyodide is the JavaScript-hosted CPython engine, including its filesystem adapter and worker transport. Python uses native CPython or WASI and has no Pyodide host adapter to mirror.
typescript_only.vfs/opfs: OPFS is the one typescript-only backend, declared in scripts/parity/parity_exceptions.json. There is no browser filesystem API for python to mirror.
typescript_only.generated: core/src/generated holds build artifacts its scripts embed (the mirage-rs wasm module, jq, quickjs, pyodide and its workers), not source modules.
typescript_only.cli/bin: An npm package declares its executable as a real file under bin/; python declares console_scripts in pyproject.toml instead.
typescript_only.server/bin: Same npm bin convention as cli/bin.
typescript_only.runtime/python/pyodide/worker: Pyodide worker transport for synchronous WASM filesystem callbacks. Python bridges WASI from a native thread and has no JavaScript worker transport.
typescript_only.runtime/python/pyodide/fs: The Emscripten filesystem adapter for Pyodide. Python uses the shared WASI host or native filesystem integration instead.
typescript_only.agents/pi: Ecosystem split: pi is an npm-only coding agent.
typescript_only.workspace/tools/read_file: Constants (the MIME tables) of the TypeScript-only read_file tool; see modules.workspace/tools.typescript_only.read_file.

python_only.imap: The asyncio IMAP4rev1 client behind accessor/email. Node's EmailAccessor drives imapflow (MIT); the asyncio IMAP client on PyPI (aioimaplib) is GPL-3.0, which an Apache-2.0 package cannot ship, so python carries its own minimal client and there is nothing on the node side to mirror.
python_only.pool: One open client per event loop, keyed by the loop object. Only python has the hazard: an aiobotocore client binds to the loop that opened it, and a process runs many loops over its lifetime (every asyncio.run makes one), so a cached client outlives the loop it belongs to and has to be released against a loop that is already closed. Node has one loop and an AWS SDK v3 client that is not bound to it, so S3Accessor there holds config and opens nothing -- there is no lifetime to manage and nothing to mirror.

typescript_only.opfs: The OPFS accessor, browser-only; see directories.typescript_only.vfs/opfs.

typescript_only.errors: QuickJsUnavailableError, raised when no qjs-wasi.wasm is found or no worker can start, which the interpreter command answers 127 for. Python raises FileNotFoundError at construction, so it has no error module.

typescript_only.immutable_set: Runtime-immutable ReadonlySet for spec data shapes; Python uses its builtin frozenset.
typescript_only.tz_abbrevs: The tzdata abbreviation table `date` renders %Z from, generated from zoneinfo by scripts/gen_tz_abbrevs.py. Python reads zoneinfo itself and has nothing to mirror; Intl offers no tzdata names, so typescript ships the data.
typescript_only.async_context: What Python's standard library already provides: AsyncLocalStorage, with a fallback for a runtime without it; Python has contextvars.
typescript_only.base64: What Python's standard library already provides: Base64 over Uint8Array for every runtime; Python has the base64 module.
typescript_only.bytes: concat for Uint8Array chunks, which commands and streams join in many places; Python joins bytes with b''.join.
typescript_only.hash: What Python's standard library already provides: SHA digests over WebCrypto or node:crypto; Python has hashlib.
typescript_only.hex: What Python's standard library already provides: Bytes to hex; Python has bytes.hex().
typescript_only.mime: What Python's standard library already provides: A byte-exact port of the corners of Python's email package (EmailMessage with policy.SMTP) that the himalaya builder rides; Python calls the email package itself.
typescript_only.normalize: What Python's standard library already provides: Maps the snake_case keys a YAML block spells onto TypeScript's camelCase config fields; Python's config fields are snake_case already.
typescript_only.optional_peer: What Python's standard library already provides: Loads an optional npm peer with an install hint; Python declares the same optional dependencies as extras and imports them where used.
typescript_only.shlex: What Python's standard library already provides: POSIX word splitting; Python has the shlex module.
typescript_only.slash: What Python's standard library already provides: Leading and trailing slash trimming; Python spells it str.strip('/').
typescript_only.sort: What Python's standard library already provides: Code-point string order; Python's str comparison is code-point order, where JavaScript's default compares UTF-16 code units.
typescript_only.text: What Python's standard library already provides: Trailing newline trimming; Python spells it str.rstrip('\n').

python_only.json_canonical: Folds integral floats in pymongo/asyncpg rows to int so json.dumps prints 1, not 1.0. JavaScript has one number type and JSON.stringify already prints 1.

typescript_only.read_file: The @openai/agents tool adapter that turns a read into an image, file or text output; the Python SDK attaches files through MirageRunner instead, so there is no tool module to mirror.
typescript_only.tools: The @openai/agents function-tool factories over the workspace tools; Python exposes its workspace tools through its SDK adapters.

python_only.runner: MirageRunner resolves a turn's multimodal attachments before Runner.run; the @openai/agents adapter returns them from its read_file tool instead.

typescript_only.client_browser: The browser transport: a page cannot hold the bot token or reach the API across CORS, so it calls through the caller's proxy (proxyUrl). Python has no browser runtime, so its client.py is the one transport.

The browser transport: a page cannot hold the bot token or reach the API across CORS, so it calls through the caller's proxy (proxyUrl). Python has no browser runtime, so its client.py is the one transport.
The browser transport: S3 commands become fetches against the caller's presigned URLs (presignedUrlProvider, itself excused in parity_exceptions.json). Python has no browser runtime.

typescript_only._driver: The driver seam core's mongodb code talks to, so node's native driver and the browser's http_driver plug into one implementation. Python has one driver (pymongo's AsyncMongoClient), which its core calls directly.
The driver seam core's postgres code talks to, so node's pg and the browser's neon_driver plug into one implementation. Python has one driver (asyncpg), which its core calls directly.

typescript_only.http_driver: The browser's mongodb driver, over the caller's HTTP proxy (see core/mongodb/_driver). Python has no browser runtime.
typescript_only.store: Node's MongoDriver over the npm mongodb driver, plugged into core/mongodb/_driver (already excused). Python's accessor/mongodb.py opens pymongo's AsyncMongoClient itself.

typescript_only.neon_driver: The browser's postgres driver, over Neon's serverless HTTP endpoint (see core/postgres/_driver). Python has no browser runtime.
typescript_only.store: Node's PgDriver over npm pg, plugged into core/postgres/_driver (already excused). Python's accessor/postgres.py opens asyncpg itself.

typescript_only.optional_peer: node's re-export of utils/optional_peer for its own optional peers, excused there, and the redis client every node store connects with (node-redis needs an error listener; Python's redis.asyncio raises on the call).
typescript_only.workspace: The per-runtime Workspace each npm runtime package exports (node and browser wire their own VFS registry, runtimes and, on node, FUSE over core's Workspace). Python has one runtime, so workspace/workspace/workspace.py is its only Workspace.

typescript_only.diff_format: Git's opcode matching and grouping helpers replace Python's standard-library difflib.SequenceMatcher. Shell diff uses the shared Rust engine; its obsolete host formatters have been removed.

python_only.xml: The ElementTree adapter: it registers the d/oc/sd namespace prefixes the query is written with and the {ns}name helpers query.py and response.py share. TypeScript writes the query from template strings with literal prefixes and parses with fast-xml-parser's removeNSPrefix, so it has no adapter to mirror.

python_only.null: NullIndexCacheStore, the do-nothing default a handler's index parameter takes. TypeScript spells the same default as an optional `index?: IndexCacheStore`, so it needs no null object.

python_only.lazyfile: dulwich reads pack data only through a seekable file object, so Python serves a mount path as a block-cached read/seek window marshalled onto the workspace loop; isomorphic-git reads packfiles through its fs client (fs.ts) and takes no file object.
python_only.objects: dulwich's object store is synchronous, so Python hand-builds a lazy BaseObjectStore over the dispatcher (loose objects fetched by id, packs opened through LazyFile, writes stored loose); isomorphic-git is async and reads loose objects and packs itself through fs.ts.

typescript_only.fs: isomorphic-git reaches a repository only through a PromiseFsClient, and this is that client over the dispatcher plus the config readers built on isomorphic-git's GitConfigManager; dulwich takes an object store and a refs container instead, which Python builds in objects.py and refs.py.
typescript_only.similarity: A port of dulwich's _similarity_score, which Python's rename detection calls directly (changes.py, diff_output.py); isomorphic-git has no rename scoring, and the two must agree digit for digit at the 60% threshold.

typescript_only.read_file: The read-file tool body (sniffs a workspace file into a text, image, PDF or binary part), shared by the npm-only vercel and opencode adapters and the openai adapter's read_file tool. No Python adapter exposes a read-file tool (openai_agents attaches files through MirageRunner), so there is nothing to mirror.

python_only.darwin: Fills macFUSE's Darwin-only fuse_operations tail (setattr_x, fsetattr_x, renamex) into mfusepy's ctypes struct, which leaves those slots NULL so FSKit creates and renames fail with ENOSYS. Node's @zkochan/fuse-native is a compiled addon with no ctypes struct to fill.

python_only.daemon: The uvicorn import target (mirage.server.daemon:app) the CLI spawns. Its twin is TypeScript's server/bin/daemon.ts, under the npm bin directory already excused as server/bin.

typescript_only.store: Node's LanceDriver (core/lancedb/query.ts) over @lancedb/lancedb. Core's accessor takes a driver, so runtime-agnostic code never imports a native npm module; Python's accessor/lancedb.py opens lancedb itself.

typescript_only.storage_id: s3StorageLocation, shared by the node and browser S3VFS classes, which are two runtime twins of Python's one vfs/s3/s3.py (where storage_location is a method). Core cannot hold the class because each runtime's accessor differs.

typescript_only.fs: Core is runtime-agnostic, so the node:fs read and write of a snapshot path load behind a runtime guard here. Python's tarfile opens the path itself inside tar_io.write_tar/read_tar.
typescript_only.types: The snapshot JSON shapes as TypeScript interfaces, so the checker can type the parsed state. Python spells the same keys as StrEnums in snapshot/keys.py and carries the state as dict[str, Any].

typescript_only.config: The browser NotionVFS's config: an MCP OAuthClientProvider for Notion's hosted MCP server, which only the browser build talks to. Python's NotionConfig is the API-key model in core/notion/config, twin of TypeScript's core/notion/config.ts.

typescript_only.constants: The node entry point's call tables (routed, refused, passthrough), the twin of runtime/python/host/constants.py, which classifies os the same way. Paired by role for the reason the fs entry gives.
typescript_only.descriptors: The descriptors the node entry point's open hands a mounted path, the twin of runtime/python/host/descriptors.py: open(2) flags onto the mode vocabulary and a table of numbers held on the null device. Paired by role for the reason the fs entry gives.
typescript_only.fs: patchNodeFs, the node twin of python's `with ws:` entry point: it swaps node's own fs and fs.promises functions onto a workspace, the way runtime/python/host patches the host interpreter's builtins.open, io.open and os functions (excused there as a directory), and both ride RuntimeFiles over ws.vfs. The two pair by role, not by path: python's entry point sits under runtime/python/host, node's under runtime/js/host, each beside the engines of its own language.
typescript_only.list: The Dirent and Dir shapes the node entry point lists a mounted directory with, the twin of runtime/python/host/list.py (MountDirEntry and MountScandir). Paired by role for the reason the fs entry gives.
typescript_only.stat: node's Stats and BigIntStats from the stat every runtime shares, the twin of runtime/python/host/stat.py (stat_result). Paired by role for the reason the fs entry gives.

python_only.build: BuildDir, the interpreter's own files routed beside the mounts, for CPython on WASI. The TypeScript host runs only qjs on WASI, which carries no files (it runs CPython through Pyodide).
python_only.slab: Puts wasmtime-py's process-wide callback slab behind a lock; a JS host has no wasmtime.

typescript_only.transport: The blocking bridge a worker guest calls the host through (shared memory, or the page's service worker), which Pyodide uses too. Python's guest runs on a thread whose calls wait on the event loop directly.
typescript_only.worker: The worker entry a guest runs on, its WasiFs answered across the bridge. Python runs the guest on a thread (WasmExecution._run_sync).
